summary: Hostile audit #9 — JOBS: phase runner, active-job tracker, run execution

survived.title: Cancel is defeated ACROSS _dispatch_active_phase's awaits — the watchdog re-sends a clean after return_to_base, then the run is finalized while the robot keeps cleaning
survived.mechanism: _run_advanced_phase checks job['_cancel_in_flight'] exactly ONCE per attempt (lines 531-549), then enters `await self._dispatch_active_phase(...)` which performs FOUR sequential awaits with no re-check: _run_global_pre_calls (Roborock: vacuum.set_fan_speed + a mop-intensity select, blocking=True cloud calls), apply_per_room_live_settings_awaited, _resolve_live_dispatch_payload (which does `await async_refresh_room_source(...)` — a full get_maps network refresh) and finally _dispatch_clean_payload. That is a multi-second-to-tens-of-seconds gap ACROSS awaits, not an intra-sync-block interleave. async_cancel_active_job (jobs/active_job.py:2203-2215) sets _cancel_in_flight synchronously and THEN awaits vacuum.return_to_base. If the user cancels inside the dispatch chain, the watchdog resumes and sends app_segment_clean / room_clean anyway — the robot turns around and starts cleaning. async_cancel_active_job's terminal-state confirm loop (line 2223) polls 30s for docked/idle, never sees it, logs only a WARNING (line 2240) and finalizes anyway; mark_active_job_finalized clears the slot. The watchdog's own _await_phase_started then sees status != 'started' and returns True, so nothing ever undoes the send.
survived.user_impact: The user presses Cancel Run, the robot returns to base, then immediately drives back out and cleans the phase's room. The job record is written as cancelled/completed and the active-job slot is cleared, so the ongoing clean is untracked, unrecorded, and no longer cancellable from the card — the user has to cancel again (or use the vacuum's own app). The window overlaps exactly the moment a user is most likely to hit Cancel: the between-room dock pause.
survived.guards_checked: phase_runner.py:531-549 (the single per-attempt _cancel_in_flight/status/phase guard — it is BEFORE the dispatch, not inside it); _dispatch_active_phase 968-1036 (no job re-read, no cancel check on any of its 4 await boundaries); dispatch/manager.py:45-84 _dispatch_clean_payload (fires the service unconditionally, no active-job inspection); dispatch/manager.py:247-323 _resolve_live_dispatch_payload (awaits async_refresh_room_source, no cancel awareness); jobs/active_job.py:2188-2247 async_cancel_active_job (sets the flag up front — correct — but its 30s non-confirmation path only WARNs and proceeds to finalize); phase_runner.py:894-904 _await_phase_started's per-poll cancel re-check (correct, but it runs AFTER the dispatch has already gone out).

survived.title: Every abnormal exit from the watchdog leaves _phase_dispatch_pending set, and that state is UN-REAPABLE BY DESIGN — the run wedges in 'started' forever and blocks all future starts
survived.mechanism: Enumerating every exit from _run_advanced_phase: (a) confirmed start -> _clear_phase_dispatch_pending, clean; (b) job advanced/finalized/paused/cancelled -> returns, guard owned elsewhere, clean; (c) attempts exhausted (line 572) -> guard LEFT SET; (d) an exception anywhere in the dispatch chain -> guard LEFT SET, task dies. For (d) the raisers are real and unguarded: _dispatch_clean_payload's `hass.services.async_call(..., blocking=True)` raises HomeAssistantError when the vacuum integration is unreachable/re-authing mid-run; _resolve_live_dispatch_payload's async_refresh_room_source can raise; dispatch_zone_clean raises ValueError on five distinct paths (no zone_command, no live map, projection validation failure, zone count cap, per-zone size bounds — dispatch/manager.py:108-172) and a zone phase's ONLY dispatch site is this task. There is no try/except anywhere in _run_advanced_phase or _dispatch_active_phase. The NEW part beyond DQ-ACT-3 is what the left-set guard costs: job_monitor.is_stranded_started (line 359) returns False the instant phase_dispatch_pending is True, so the stranded-job reaper is explicitly disabled; listeners/lifecycle.py:297 sets should_finalize_completed = False on the same flag, so the completion gate is disabled; and advance_active_job_phase (queue_engine.py:476) had already reset has_observed_active_lifecycle to False, which is a SECOND independent block on both the completion gate (lifecycle.py:269) and the reaper (job_monitor.py:357). The job therefore sits status='started' permanently, and evaluate_job_lifecycle then returns 'active_job_running' -> build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle blocks EVERY subsequent start.
survived.user_impact: One transient service failure (or a zone phase whose live map isn't loaded) permanently kills the run AND every future run: the card shows a job forever 'in progress' on a parked robot, scheduled/automated starts are blocked with 'A room-clean job is currently active', and nothing recovers it — not the reaper, not the completion gate, not an HA restart's normal path. Only a manual Cancel Run clears it. On Roborock nothing surfaces the stall at all (see guards), so the user's only symptom is that cleaning silently stopped happening.

survived.mechanism: `has_native = bool(cfg.get('entities', {}).get('active_cleaning_target'))` tests whether the adapter DECLARED an entity id, not whether that entity exists or whether the signal is a trustworthy live current-room source. The right question already exists elsewhere in the codebase: live_transition.native_transition_source, which Roborock sets True (adapter.py:474) and Eufy explicitly sets False (adapter.py:753). jobs/active_job.py:951 uses that flag to decide whether to trust the same resolver; the watchdog does not. docs/dev/design/eufy-native-transition.md:34-39 states outright that Eufy's active_cleaning_target is a completion SENTINEL of the wrong shape and that a 'name-surfacing + slug-reconciliation shim' is a PREREQUISITE that has not been built. survived.user_impact: On a Eufy 'vacuum -> charge to 80% -> mop' profile, the mop phase is re-dispatched up to 3 times, 90 seconds apart, while the robot is already mopping — each room_clean restarts the clean, so the robot repeatedly abandons and restarts the same rooms. survived.title: An HA restart during a room_group or zone phase's un-confirmed window strands the run — the re-arm covers ONLY dock phases and the comment's claimed recovery path cannot fire
survived.mechanism: core/manager.py:332-336 force-clears _phase_dispatch_pending on every loaded job, then core/manager.py:473-480 re-arms via rearm_dock_phase_if_needed, which returns False at line 125 for anything that is not is_dock_polled_phase_type (i.e. everything except charge_wait/wait). The comment at manager.py:325-326 claims 'a ROOM-group run then advances via the normal completion path (or Cancel Run)' — that is a claim the code does not have. A persisted _phase_dispatch_pending == True means precisely that the watchdog had NOT yet confirmed the phase started, i.e. the robot is parked in the settle window (10s, or 45s for a dock-room target) or in a verify window where the dispatch was ignored. advance_active_job_phase already reset has_observed_active_lifecycle to False (queue_engine.py:476), and listeners/lifecycle.py:269 requires it for should_finalize_completed while lifecycle.py:200-202 can only re-arm it when the lifecycle reads active (and, on Roborock, when is_job_active is ON). A parked robot satisfies neither. The reaper is likewise blocked by job_monitor.py:357 on the same flag. Nothing re-spawns _run_advanced_phase for the phase, so the segment command is never sent.
survived.user_impact: Restart HA (or reload the integration) while a phased run is between rooms, and the run stops dead: the robot never leaves the dock, the card shows the job still 'started' forever, no error and no log line is emitted, the reaper never fires, and every future start is blocked with 'A room-clean job is currently active' until the user manually cancels.

survived.title: Adapter-declared phase_timing overrides are applied with no clamping — poll_seconds: 0 pins the event loop in a hot loop, max_attempts: 0 dispatches nothing and wedges the phase
survived.mechanism: core/manager.py:4904-4912 merges dispatch.phase_timing straight over the defaults with only a type coercion (`type(pt[key])(declared[key])`) and no range check; adapters/config_schema.py:969-973 declares phase_timing as an unvalidated free-form dict. phase_runner.py:891 then does `_poll = float(pt['poll_seconds'])` and phase_runner.py:966 does `await asyncio.sleep(_poll)`. With poll_seconds: 0 the loop yields but never advances its accounting — cleaning_in_target and idle both increment by 0.0, so neither `>= confirm_seconds` nor `>= verify_seconds` can ever be reached and _await_phase_started spins the event loop indefinitely at full CPU with no exit. With max_attempts: 0 (or negative) `range(1, 1)` is empty, so _run_advanced_phase performs ZERO dispatches and falls straight through to the give-up log at 572, leaving _phase_dispatch_pending set — the WD-2 permanent wedge, reached without a single command being sent. A negative verify_seconds makes every attempt fail on the first poll, burning all three re-dispatches immediately.
survived.user_impact: A future brand adapter (the seam exists precisely so a third path-optimizing brand can declare its own profile) that ships a typo or a deliberate 0 either freezes Home Assistant's event loop for every integration on the box, or silently disables phase dispatch entirely. Neither shipped adapter trips it today — Eufy declares no phase_timing block and Roborock's values are sane — so this is a seam defect, not a live bug.

survived.title: Cancel is LOST across _dispatch_active_phase's awaits — the watchdog re-sends a clean AFTER return_to_base and the robot is left cleaning with no job record

survived.title: Cancelling a sequenced run reports the WRONG missed rooms — per-phase reset of queue_room_ids/completed_room_ids feeds the incomplete-run log and trouble-rooms counters
survived.mechanism: `advance_active_job_phase` REPLACES `queue_room_ids` with only the next phase's rooms and RESETS `completed_room_ids`/`completed_rooms` to [] on every advance (queue/queue_engine.py:463, 467-468). `async_cancel_active_job` finalizes with `forced_outcome_status='cancelled'`, and the finalizer reads the LIVE record (`active_job_state = manager.get_active_job(...)`, learning/job_finalizer.py:469-472). `_write_incomplete_run_log` then computes `missed_room_ids = set(queued_room_ids) - set(active_completed)` from exactly those two per-phase fields (job_finalizer.py:1505-1522), and `_update_trouble_rooms_log` does the same (:1603-1622). The rescue at job_finalizer.py:752-761 that synthesizes the full queue applies ONLY to `outcome_status == 'completed'`, explicitly not to cancelled. Two distinct wrong outcomes: (a) cancel during a room_group phase N>0 -> `queued_room_ids` is only phase N's room(s), so every room in phases N+1..end that was never cleaned is silently ABSENT from the missed list; (b) cancel during a charge_wait/wait/zone phase -> that phase carries `queue_room_ids: []` (planning/run_plan.py:851, 858, 878), which triggers the fallback at job_finalizer.py:332-333 to the LIVE map queue (the full original selection) while `completed_room_ids` is still [], so EVERY room in the run is reported missed including the ones phase 0 actually cleaned. Case (b) is the documented path: `_run_charge_wait_phase`'s docstring (phase_runner.py:596-597) claims the timeout 'finalize[s] like a cancel, so the un-cleaned remaining rooms are reported missed' — a comment asserting behaviour the code does not have.

survived.title: Cancel OPENS the completion gate it is about to wait for — it clears _phase_dispatch_pending before return_to_base, and neither the gate nor maybe_advance_phase checks _cancel_in_flight
survived.mechanism: `async_cancel_active_job` sets `_phase_dispatch_pending = False` (active_job.py:2205) BEFORE issuing return_to_base, then spends up to 30 s awaiting the device to reach docked/idle/task_status=completed (:2210-2237). That flag is the ONLY thing stopping the lifecycle completion gate from acting on a between-phase dock (listeners/lifecycle.py:297-298). The job's status stays 'started' for the whole window, so the listener's filter at lifecycle.py:137 admits it, and `should_finalize_completed` (lifecycle.py:263-284) is evaluated as a LEVEL check on the exact signals the cancel is driving the robot toward. Neither lifecycle.py:300-312 nor `PhaseRunner.maybe_advance_phase` (phase_runner.py:141-200) checks `_cancel_in_flight` at all. Consequences: (a) mid-sequence -> `advance_active_job_phase` runs, incrementing `current_phase_index` and wiping `completed_room_ids`/`completed_rooms` (feeding CAN-2); (b) on the LAST phase, and for every ATOMIC job, `maybe_advance_phase` returns False and the listener calls `finalize_learning_for_active_job` with NO forced status (lifecycle.py:316-321) — it takes the exactly-once claim first, so the run is written as a normal COMPLETED run with used_for_learning=True and the cancel's own forced 'cancelled' finalize gets 'already_finalized'/'finalize_in_flight'. The heuristic cancel detector cannot rescue (b): `_detect_cancel_likely_run` bails with 'not_single_room' unless `len(resolved_rooms) == 1` (job_finalizer.py:1326-1328). Worst reachability is Roborock: `completion.task_status_value` is 'charging' (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:263), so during a charge_wait phase the robot is LITERALLY sitting in the completion state — and the charge-timeout auto-cancel at phase_runner.py:696 routes through this same function, clearing the guard while the robot charges on the dock.
survived.user_impact: A cancelled or charge-timed-out run is recorded as a successful full completion and fed into the learning set, so a truncated run's room timings/areas/battery deltas become the learned baseline. The user gets no cancelled record, no incomplete-run banner and no EVENT_RUN_INCOMPLETE, and the active-job snapshot's finalize_summary is then blanked to all-None when the cancel's own `mark_active_job_finalized` runs with the rejected result.

survived.title: Pause+resume permanently kills the phase watchdog for room_group and zone phases — resume re-arms ONLY dock phases and never restores the dispatch guard
survived.mechanism: `pause_active_job` flips status to 'paused' and clears `_phase_dispatch_pending` (active_job.py:1900-1906). On the next poll the live watchdog `_run_advanced_phase` sees `status != 'started'` and RETURNS permanently (phase_runner.py:536-549) — likewise `_await_phase_started` returns True and exits (phase_runner.py:898-904). `async_resume_active_job` restores only status/paused_at/paused_duration (active_job.py:1941-1943) and then calls `rearm_dock_phase_if_needed` (:2155), which bails at phase_runner.py:125 via `is_dock_polled_phase_type` — DOCK_POLLED_PHASE_TYPES is {'charge_wait','wait'} only, deliberately excluding 'zone' and never containing 'room_group' (step_types.py:41). So for a room_group or zone phase, resume re-arms NOTHING and does not restore the guard. The phase is left with no driver, no retry budget and no gate suppression. This matters because the watchdog's whole purpose is re-sending an `app_segment_clean` the device IGNORED (phase_runner.py:7-12): if the pause lands inside the settle/verify window — up to `settle 10 s` (or `dock_settle 45 s`) plus 3 x `verify 90 s` ~= 4.5 min of every phase (core/manager.py:74-99) — the room may never have started, and after resume nothing will ever re-dispatch it. `vacuum.start` (active_job.py:2136-2141) resumes the device's own last command, not our segment target. With `_phase_dispatch_pending` now False, the robot's dock state satisfies the completion gate and `maybe_advance_phase` walks straight past the un-started phase. For a ZONE phase this is sharper still: a zone is dispatched ONLY by `_dispatch_active_phase`'s zone branch (phase_runner.py:996-1008), so the whole zone clean is skipped.
survived.user_impact: A pause+resume during a stepped run silently skips a room or an entire saved-zone step, and the run then finalizes as a normal successful completion (the guard that would have stalled it is gone). The user sees a clean 'completed' record for a run that never touched one of its rooms. The in-code comment at active_job.py:2146-2148 asserts the opposite — 'a ROOM-group phase resumes guard-free and the completion gate advances normally' — which is true only when the robot actually IS cleaning that room, exactly the condition the watchdog exists to verify.

survived.title: A dispatched run the device never started can never be reaped, then the NEXT run's completion signals finalize the stale slot with the wrong run's data

Second-order damage: `maybe_handle_external_run` refuses to open a capture slot while ANY map holds status started/paused (external_run.py:87-96), so the stale slot suppresses external capture. survived.title: async_finalize_stranded_job reports success regardless of the finalizer's answer — a refused finalize still marks the slot 'completed' and fires a bogus EVENT_JOB_FINISHED
survived.mechanism: `async_finalize_stranded_job` never inspects `finalize_result`. It passes whatever came back to `mark_active_job_finalized` and unconditionally returns `{"finalized": True, ...}`. Three refusal shapes reach it: `{"finalized": False, "reason": "finalize_in_flight"}` and `{... "already_finalized"}` from the exactly-once claim (learning/manager.py:704-716), and plain `None` when `_get_learning_manager()` is None (core/manager.py:4634-4635) or `{... "missing_started_at"}` (4645-4651). `mark_active_job_finalized` then sets status='completed', finalized=True and a finalize_summary of all-None (active_job.py:2034-2076) — labelling an unrecorded interrupted run 'completed'. The listener at pause_timeout.py:124 checks only `result.get("finalized")`, so it fires EVENT_JOB_FINISHED, and `job_finished_event_data` DEFAULTS the payload status to 'completed' when the outcome dict is empty (_common.py:229). The `finalize_in_flight` refusal is reachable because the reaper tick has no overlap guard: `async_track_time_interval(..., timedelta(minutes=1))` re-enters `hass.async_create_task(_process())` (pause_timeout.py:155-161) whether or not the previous `_process` finished, and `_process` can exceed 60s — `async_cancel_active_job` alone holds a hard 30s terminal-confirm poll (`_CANCEL_CONFIRM_TIMEOUT_S`, active_job.py:2218-2237) per paused job, before a `rebuild_stats=True` finalize, iterated over every vacuum and every map id.

survived.title: The vacuum-state busy branch is unreachable for every HA-standard vacuum state — an errored or externally-cleaning robot classifies as "ready" and Start dispatches at it
survived.mechanism: The final busy check is `if vacuum_state_n not in {"", "docked", "idle", "paused"} and vacuum_state_n not in active_vacuum_states`. `active_vacuum_states` defaults to `_HA_ACTIVE_VACUUM_STATES` = {cleaning, returning, paused, error} (job_monitor.py:10-15). The HA vacuum platform's activity enum has exactly six values — cleaning, docked, idle, paused, returning, error — and `_norm()` folds unavailable/unknown to "". The union of the two exemption sets therefore covers EVERY state the entity can report, so this branch can never fire in production; the same set is used at line 200 as EVIDENCE OF ACTIVITY and at line 217 as an EXEMPTION FROM BUSY, meaning the exact states it exists to catch are the ones it lets through. Because line 197's `active_cleaning_target` / active-state test is gated behind `active_job_exists`, the only remaining defence for an UNTRACKED run is line 209 (`task_status_n in active_run_task_states`). Roborock's `ACTIVE_RUN_TASK_STATES` (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:16-26) contains no "error", "paused" or "idle", and that module's own docstring records `error` (plus `bumper_stuck` / `wheels_suspended`) as live-observed `sensor.ivy_status` values. So: robot stuck mid-floor after an app-started run -> vacuum.ivy="error", sensor.ivy_status="error", no framework-tracked job -> line 180/188 skipped (Roborock declares hard_service_states=[] and drying_states=[]), line 197 skipped (no active job), line 209 skipped, line 217 exempted -> returns lifecycle_state="ready", message "Ready to start cleaning.", blocking=False. The same falls out for vacuum_state="paused" on either brand ("paused" sits in BOTH exemption sets, and Eufy's ACTIVE_RUN_TASK_STATES has no "paused").
survived.user_impact: The card shows "Ready to start cleaning." and an enabled Start button while the robot is sitting on the floor in an error/stuck state or paused mid-run. Pressing Start passes the only start gate and dispatches a real clean command (app_segment_clean / room clean) at a robot that is faulted or already mid-run, on top of a run the framework is not tracking.

survived.title: invalid_payload uses phase 0's room count as the whole run's room count — a saved run profile whose first step is a zone is accepted on save but can never start
survived.mechanism: `if int(payload_room_count or 0) <= 0: return {"reason": "invalid_payload", ...}`. The caller passes `payload_room_count=int(payload_state.get("room_count", 0))` (core/manager.py:2863) where `payload_state = start_plan["payload_state"]`, and for a STEPPED run `_build_effective_start_plan` sets `payload_state = phases[0]` (planning/run_plan.py:1379). `_build_steps_phases` pops leading/trailing break phases, but `_BREAKS = ("charge_wait", "wait")` only (planning/run_plan.py:883-887) — a `zone` phase is deliberately NOT a break ("A zone is a real clean phase", line 895) and is emitted with `"payload": {}, "room_count": 0` (line 873-879). So for a profile whose steps are [zone, room_group], phases[0] is the zone phase, payload_room_count == 0, and build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle returns blocked=True / "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid." before it ever looks at the lifecycle state. `set_run_profile_steps` accepts this profile: its only structural guard is `if not any(s.get("type") == "room_group" for s in normalized)` (profiles/manager.py:1015) — it requires a room_group to EXIST, not to come first, and `normalize_run_profile_steps` (profiles/manager.py:798-808) accepts a zone step in any position. The phase runner explicitly expects this shape: `_snapshot_zone_timing`'s docstring says the start is "the run start for a leading zone" (jobs/phase_runner.py:341). start_run_profile then deletes the stashed steps because the run did not start (profiles/manager.py:1341-1345), so the next plain Start is a flat clean.
survived.user_impact: A user saves a run profile like "clean the hallway zone first, then the bedrooms", presses its exposed button, and gets "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid." every time, with rooms visibly selected and a valid queue. Nothing names the real cause (the step ordering); the profile is permanently unstartable and the only fix is reordering steps the UI never said were order-constrained.

is_stranded_started() vacuum-state requirement (job_monitor.py:361) — requiring docked/idle correctly leaves a still-'returning' run and an 'error' run alone; the docstring's stated reasoning (reaping a maybe-recovering run is worse than a lingering record) matches the code.

stranded_since stamp/clear lifecycle (active_job.py:2331-2413) — the stamp is written on the first holding tick and _clear_stranded_stamp fires on ANY non-strand tick and on any non-'started' status, so a transient dock genuinely cannot accrue grace. All mutation happens in one synchronous block before any await, so it is atomic under HA's single loop.
stranded_since is persisted and survives a restart, so a strand that began before an HA restart correctly resumes its grace clock instead of restarting it.

get_paused_job_timeout_report (active_job.py:2286-2329) — pure and correct: status gate, pause_timeout_minutes<=0 opt-out, None on unparseable paused_at/now, elapsed clamped at 0, and the returned report carries the exact forced lifecycle state/message the cancel path needs.

Restart recovery of both persisted guards is correct and unconditional: async_initialize clears every stale _phase_dispatch_pending on load (core/manager.py:332-336) and _clear_orphaned_finalize_claims drops every orphaned finalize_claimed_at (484-508), with a correct written rationale for why an age heuristic is unnecessary.

rearm_dock_phase_if_needed + _spawn_dock_poller (phase_runner.py:77-139) — the (vac, map, phase_index) key genuinely prevents a normal advance and a restart re-arm from double-driving one dock phase, and keying on phase_index (not just vac/map) correctly lets a poller advancing to the next dock phase spawn its successor before its own finally releases the old key.

_run_wait_phase_impl deadline reconstruction (phase_runner.py:783-812) — a restart mid-wait recomputes remaining time from the persisted wait_started_at instead of restarting the full timer, and clamps an already-elapsed wait to 0.

The exactly-once finalize claim at the chokepoint (learning/manager.py:690-741) — correctly placed below both entry points, written synchronously before the first await, released in a finally on every exit path, with `finalized` as the permanent gate so the release cannot reopen it. It does prevent a duplicate learning RECORD even when the reaper double-fires.

_normalize_active_job (active_job.py:314-356) is a key-preserving shallow copy plus setdefaults, so persisting a normalized copy back via _persist_active_job does not drop _cancel_in_flight, phase keys, counter_samples or finalize_claimed_at.

Roborock mid-run recharge is correctly excluded from the strand definition: is_job_active(unavailable_is_active=True) keeps the job-active binary asserted through the recharge dock and treats a transient unavailable/unknown as still active (_common.py:110-143).

async_cancel_active_job's ordering (active_job.py:2198-2276) — setting _cancel_in_flight and clearing _phase_dispatch_pending on the STORED record before return_to_base, and wrapping the finalize so the clear always happens, is the correct shape; the defect in STR-2 is that the stranded twin does not copy it.

build_active_job_state (queue/queue_engine.py:366-426) returns a fresh dict, so no stale _cancel_in_flight / _phase_dispatch_pending / stranded_since from a previous run can carry into a new job on the same slot.

Interrupted outcomes are correctly held out of learning: history_store.py:914-924 appends job_interrupted to learning_blockers and forces used_for_learning=False, and job_finalizer.py:977 gates the cumulative battery push on it — so an inflated ended_at on a reaped run cannot poison learned room times.

is_stranded_started (job_monitor.py:320-369) — all five exclusions verified against the live caller (jobs/active_job.py:2339-2423). Specifically chased the charge-wait reap hypothesis: _phase_dispatch_pending is held for the ENTIRE duration of a charge_wait/wait phase (phase_runner.py:589 and 733 both state it, and rearm_dock_phase_if_needed re-asserts it after an HA restart at phase_runner.py:129-130), so a 3-hour charge wait cannot accrue the 5-minute strand grace. Correct.

is_stranded_started's job_active_on input — is_job_active returns False early when the adapter declares no entities.job_active (listeners/_common.py:135-136), so the unavailable_is_active=True passed at active_job.py:2392 cannot become a permanent True on Eufy and silently kill the FN-1 reaper for that brand. Genuinely brand-agnostic.

poll_stranded_started_job's stamp lifecycle — _clear_stranded_stamp fires on every non-stranded tick and on any status != started (active_job.py:2365-2367, 2396-2398), so a transient dock cannot accumulate grace across a resume.

evaluate_job_lifecycle precedence ladder for map_mismatch > hard_service > drying — matches the docstring's claim that drying is warning-only while washing/recycling/emptying hard-block; verified against both adapters' vocabulary and test [JM-20].

_norm (job_monitor.py:86-91) — the unknown/unavailable/none -> "" sentinel folding is applied consistently to all four state inputs; active_map_id/selected_map_id are deliberately NOT normed, which makes an unavailable active-map entity fail toward map_mismatch (blocking) rather than toward ready. Conservative in the right direction.

build_job_metadata_from_payload (job_monitor.py:94-135) — non-list resolved_rooms, non-dict payload, non-dict room entries and unparseable room_ids are all coerced or skipped without raising; no path can reach int() with a bad value.

build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle branch coverage — enumerated every lifecycle_state evaluate_job_lifecycle can return {map_mismatch, mid_job_service, dock_drying, active_job_running, vacuum_busy, ready}; each has a handler except map_mismatch, which is independently re-derived from the same two map-id inputs at lines 254-259, so the missing explicit branch is not a hole.

BlockedRoomEntry blocked-by attribution (planning/run_plan.py:1161-1181) — chased the "blocker names the wrong room" hypothesis and it does not hold: the accessibility propagation loop guarantees that if a child is inaccessible then no parent of it is accessible, so the next() predicate cannot select an accessible parent, and the parent_ids[0] fallback is effectively dead. The named room is either correct or None (when the blocking parent is unselected, since the lookup uses selected_rooms_by_id) — never a different, non-blocking room.

_pending_run_steps peek-vs-pop discipline (planning/run_plan.py:1330-1338, profiles/manager.py:1334-1345) — preflight callers PEEK and only the real dispatch POPs, and the failed-start path deletes the leftover stash, so a preflight cannot eat the stash and a blocked start cannot leak it into the next plain Start.
verifier_notes:
28 of 30 survived; 2 killed. Verification was source-level in every case — I read phase_runner.py end to end, active_job.py's cancel/pause/recharge/recorder/strand regions, all of job_monitor.py, listeners/lifecycle.py, listeners/pause_timeout.py, listeners/_common.py, listeners/job_metrics.py, queue/queue_engine.py, planning/run_plan.py, dispatch/manager.py, learning/manager.py's exactly-once claim, learning/job_finalizer.py's incomplete-run writers, counter_segmentation.py, and both adapters plus their vocabularies.

KILLS (2):
- A3-REC-6: the learned-area fallback is unreachable in production. `_learned_room_area_m2` reads a room-record key no writer ever sets — grep shows `learned_area_m2` written only into a transient scoring dict (learning/external_ingest.py:243/:464) and the managed-room store carries no area at all (rooms/room_discovery.py:249-255, rooms/room_manager.py, rooms/room_crud.py). The learned area lives in room_stats.avg_area_m2. The only proof of the described behaviour is a test that hand-seeds the key.
- A3-REC-7: the premise (counters reset at a PHASE boundary) is not established. The cited counter_segmentation._prepare_window comment is explicitly about a reset carried over from the previous JOB. Without a per-phase reset there is no negative delta to clamp, and the knock-on to REC-6 fails independently.

SEVERITY CORRECTIONS (4):
- A1-WD-2 CRITICAL→HIGH: "blocks EVERY subsequent start" is refuted on Eufy (a parked robot with a cleared active_cleaning_target evaluates to 'ready'; get_start_status blocks only on status=='paused'), holds only on Roborock whose current_room reverts to the dock room NAME. Cancel Run also recovers, so "unrecoverable" is overstated. The un-reapable wedge itself is fully confirmed.
- A2-CAN-4 HIGH→MEDIUM: the harm needs the pause to land in the un-confirmed window AND the device to have ignored the dispatch; otherwise the comment's claim holds.
- A4-AJ-2 HIGH→MEDIUM: aligned with its duplicate REC-4; needs a multi-map install plus a stale bucket.
- A5-STR-1 CRITICAL→MEDIUM: the dock_status-discarded asymmetry is real in source, but no source establishes a reachable state where a Eufy dock service cycle leaves task_status outside external_mid_run_statuses — that set has entries for all three parking cycles (mop wash, dust empty, recharge), and the uncovered strings are dock_status values belonging to those same cycles. Needs a captured trace before it ships as CRITICAL.

DUPLICATE CLUSTERS the orchestrator should collapse to one work item each:
1. A1-WD-1 == A2-CAN-1 (cancel lost across _dispatch_active_phase's four awaits) — same file, same lines, same fix.
2. A1-WD-2 == A5-STR-3 (watchdog give-up/raise leaves _phase_dispatch_pending set; both consumers treat it as a permanent veto). STR-3 states the recovery correctly; prefer its framing.
3. A2-CAN-3 == A4-AJ-3 (cancel clears the guard the completion gate honours). AJ-3 has the more precise mechanism; CAN-3 adds the last-phase/atomic finalize consequence — but note CAN-3's "every ATOMIC job" is wrong (active_job.py:2203 gates on phases) and its "worst reachability = charge_wait" is wrong (has_observed_active_lifecycle cannot re-arm on a docked Roborock).
4. A3-REC-4 == A4-AJ-2 (the two sample recorders' repudiated predicate + per-map fan-out).

CROSS-FINDING INTERACTION worth flagging: A3-REC-3 (completed_room_ids is always [] on a phased job) is what makes A2-CAN-2's under-reporting unconditional rather than occasional — fixing REC-3 changes CAN-2's failure mode, so sequence them together.

Two structural observations that emerged while refuting, offered as leads rather than findings: (1) `_phase_dispatch_pending` is written as a transient marker and read as a permanent veto by three independent consumers with no age or expiry anywhere — that shape, not any single exit path, is the actual defect class behind WD-2/WD-4/CAN-4/STR-3; (2) `_cancel_in_flight` is honoured by exactly the three call sites that were patched for it (_run_advanced_phase, both dock pollers' `_still_ours`) and by nothing that was written earlier — the completion gate, maybe_advance_phase, advance_active_job_phase and _dispatch_active_phase all carry it forward unread.

All 30 findings reproduce against the source; none is a false positive. Ten severities corrected, all downward — the finders inflated on impact, not on mechanism.

DUPLICATES (same defect, reported by two areas — should be merged before triage):
- A1-WD-1 == A2-CAN-1 (cancel lost across _dispatch_active_phase's awaits)
- A1-WD-2 == A5-STR-3 (_phase_dispatch_pending left set is an un-reapable wedge)
- A3-REC-4 == A4-AJ-2 (the two sample recorders' repudiated predicate)
- A2-CAN-3 and A4-AJ-3 are two halves of ONE defect: the completion gate has no _cancel_in_flight check and the cancel itself clears the guard. AJ-3 states it more precisely.

FACTUAL ERRORS INSIDE OTHERWISE-REAL FINDINGS (fix these in the report, they will mislead the fixer):
1. A2-CAN-3 "and for every ATOMIC job" is wrong. active_job.py:2203 gates the whole guard-clear on `if active_job.get('phases')`, so an atomic job never had the guard set and the cancel opens nothing. Only the phased path is caused by the cancel.
2. A2-CAN-4's stated outcome is wrong. It does NOT finalize as a successful completion — advance_active_job_phase already set has_observed_active_lifecycle=False and a parked robot cannot re-arm it, so the completion gate stays shut and the run WEDGES (and the reaper is blind on the same flag). Bad, but a different failure than described.
3. A5-STR-4's "no automatic path can clear it" is too strong. Because lifecycle reads 'ready' for the phantom job, a new dispatched Start is not blocked and overwrites the slot. The damage window is bounded by the next Start.
4. A1-WD-4 overstates the trigger. A persisted pending guard usually means the robot IS cleaning but is unconfirmed, in which case the restart is harmless and the manager.py:325-326 comment is correct. The real failure needs the restart inside the settle window or a verify window where the device ignored the dispatch.

WEAKEST FINDING — A5-STR-1, downgraded CRITICAL -> MEDIUM. Two load-bearing premises are asserted without source support: that a Eufy dock service cycle clears active_cleaning_target (if it does not, completion_secondary_satisfied returns False and is_stranded_started bails), and that 'Recycling waste water' can arrive as task_status (the adapter records external_mid_run_statuses as verified against robovac_mqtt's _map_task_status, while HARD_SERVICE_STATES deliberately mixes dock_status and task_status vocabularies). What IS provable and worth fixing: completed_finalize_signals returns dock_status and poll_stranded_started_job discards it, while the sibling evaluate_job_lifecycle in the same file checks BOTH entities against the wider set.

STRONGEST FINDING — A4-AJ-1. Structurally unreachable code proven by two independent routes, plus a test at tests/integration/test_jobs_active_job.py:250-269 that is green only because it monkeypatches one pure hass.states read to return two different values, with a comment naming both call sites. That test is itself the artifact that let the dead branch ship.

CROSS-CUTTING ROOT CAUSES worth noting for the fix plan — the 30 findings collapse onto four seams:
(a) _phase_dispatch_pending is a transient marker consumed as a permanent veto by two independent gates (WD-2/STR-3/STR-4/CAN-3/AJ-3/CAN-4/WD-4).
(b) _cancel_in_flight is asked by the watchdog and the dock pollers but never by the completion gate, maybe_advance_phase, or anything inside the dispatch chain (WD-1/CAN-1/CAN-3/AJ-3), and pause has no equivalent flag at all (CAN-5).
(c) per-phase recording assumes one phase = one room, which is false on Eufy where honors_clean_order folds strict order off (REC-1/REC-2/REC-3), and phase 0's queue is never narrowed.
(d) a declared-but-unwritten / written-but-unread field family: last_battery_percent (read, never written), area_source (written, never read), available (declared, never honoured), source='access_graph' (documented, never written), ended_at (predicated on, never written).
